help.title: Help
help.subtitle: How the panel works, every command and who can do what.
help.panelHint: Everything you can do from here.

player.title: Now playing
player.body: Cover, title, artists, who asked for it and the genres when they are known. Below: the position slider, previous, play or pause, next, loop (off, queue, track), shuffle and volume. Stop clears the queue after a confirmation.

queue.title: Queue
queue.body: Paste a link or search to add songs. Drag the handle to reorder, use the cross to remove a song and Clear to empty the queue. History lists the last songs played and lets you add one again.

playlists.title: Playlists
playlists.body: Every playlist, album or artist page you add with /play or in the Queue tab is saved here for you, on any server. Open one to see its songs, add them all or one by one. Pin the ones you want to keep on top; when the list is full the oldest unpinned one makes room. Songs are refreshed at most every hour; Refresh data from playlist reads it again now (once every few seconds).

lyrics.title: Lyrics
lyrics.body: Lyrics come from LRCLIB. Synced lyrics highlight the current line and follow the song; tap a line to jump to it. Some songs only have plain lyrics, and some have none.

radio.title: Radio
radio.body: Starts an endless mix from your history, your likes and similar listeners. You can add a short prompt such as "calm music to study". While it picks songs, the queue shows each step and you can cancel it. At the bottom, Your taste shows your top genres: click one to see its songs and remove the ones you do not want on your radio.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body: Only for server managers: control mode, the DJ list, the Lynx channel and channel rules, vote to skip, the queue limit and the default volume.

privacy.title: Account
privacy.body: The round button with your picture, top right: theme and accent color, language, your listening history and deleting your data. Your taste is at the bottom of the Radio tab.

language.title: Language
language.body: Change it in your account (top right). It changes the panel language for you only. The bot's messages in the channel keep the server's language.

jam.title: Jam
jam.body: Invite to jam (in the panel or on the Now playing message) shares a link. Whoever opens it gets the panel in their own voice channel and can join: every channel plays the same queue at the same position, and the volume stays per channel. The host channel decides who may join (other channels of the server, other servers), who edits the shared queue, closes the jam, removes channels or ends it. Joining saves your channel's own queue; it comes back when you leave or the jam ends. If the host channel empties, the host role passes to the channel that joined first. Jams are not kept across a Lynx restart: each channel resumes its own queue.

help.seekNote: Moving to a point in the song is only possible here, with the slider. There is no seek command.
help.feedbackNote: Like and Dislike tune your radio: a dislike keeps that song out of your mixes.
help.commandsHint: Type them in any text channel of the server while you are in a voice channel.

play.description: Joins your voice channel and plays a link (YouTube, YouTube Music, Spotify track, album or playlist) or the best match for a search.

skip.description: Skips to the next song. When vote to skip is on, your use counts as a vote.

stop.description: Stops the music, clears the queue and leaves the channel.

nowplaying.description: Shows the current song with its position.

remove.description: Removes a song by its position in the queue. Without control you can only remove your own.

move.description: Moves a song to another position in the queue.

skipto.description: Jumps straight to a song in the queue, dropping the ones before it.

loop.description: Sets the loop mode: off, track or queue.

volume.description: Sets the volume from 10 to 100. 100 plays the audio untouched.

lyrics.description: Shows the lyrics of the current song.

invite.description: Shows a link to add Lynx to another server, plus the support server and website when they are set.

about.description: Shows the version, uptime, gateway ping, how many servers and voice channels Lynx is in, and links to the source code.

ai.description: Starts the AI radio, with an optional prompt. Use it again or /stop to end it.

help.accessNote: Control means the command follows the server's control mode. Vote means it can need votes from the channel.
help.permissionsHint: Checked by the bot on every action, in the panel and in commands.

manager.title: Lynx manager
manager.body: The server owner and anyone with Administrator or Manage Server. Managers can always control playback and are the only ones who see Settings.

dj.title: DJ
dj.body: People a manager added to the DJ list in Settings. It is a Lynx list, not a Discord role. DJs control playback in any mode and skip without votes.

modes.title: Control modes
modes.everyone: Everyone (default): anyone in the voice channel can pause, skip, seek, reorder and remove songs.
modes.dj: DJs only: only DJs and managers control playback. Everyone else can add songs and remove their own.

vote.title: Vote to skip
vote.body: Off by default. When a manager turns it on, a skip needs a set number or share of votes from the people listening. DJs and managers skip right away.

support.title: Thanks for using Lynx!
support.body: Lynx is free and its source code is public. If it makes your listening sessions a little better, consider dropping a star on GitHub: it really helps the project grow. Ideas, bug reports and pull requests are always welcome too.

stored.title: What is stored
items: The last 2000 different songs you requested: title, artist, link, how many times you played each one and when you last played it.
The playlists and albums you add (name, image, platform and link), for the Playlists tab.

used.title: What it is used for
items: Your AI radio and your genre taste.
Finding listeners with a similar taste across servers, anonymously.
It is never shown to other users.

off.title: When it is off
items: Like, Dislike and /ai are turned off for you.
You are left out of other people's recommendations.
New playlists are not saved to your Playlists tab.

danger.title: Danger zone
danger.body: Deleting is immediate and cannot be undone. This removes:
items: Your listening history (every song, play count and date).
Your taste profile (genres and radio data).
Your similarity links with other listeners, in both directions.
itemsNoAi: Anything Lynx stored about your listening.
danger.kept: Your panel settings (language, theme, accent and the history switch) are kept.

jam.title: Jam
jam.startBody: Play the same music in other voice channels at the same time.
jam.startHint: Share the link: whoever opens it gets the panel in their own voice channel and can join. Every channel hears the same song at the same position; volume stays per channel.
jam.readOnly: Only people in {{name}} can change these.
jam.allowChannelsHint: Voice channels of the host's server may join.
jam.allowServersHint: Voice channels of other servers may join.
jam.editableByHint: Each server's DJ mode still applies.
jam.closedHint: Channels already in the jam stay.
jam.hostOnlyNotice: Only people in {{name}} can change the music. You can still set the volume here.
jam.endQuestion: Every channel goes back to its own queue. End it?
jam.leaveQuestion: Your channel gets its own queue back. Leave?
jam.joinBody: {{channel}} will play the jam's music at the same time as the others. Its own queue is saved and comes back when it leaves.

controlMode.body: Decides who can pause, skip, seek, change the loop, reorder and remove songs. With Everyone (the default), anyone in the voice channel can. With DJs only, just DJs and managers can; everyone else can still add songs and remove the ones they added. Managers (owner, Administrator or Manage Server) can always control, even from outside the channel.
controlMode.example: You pick DJs only and add Ana to the DJ list. Ana and the managers can skip and reorder; Leo, who is not a DJ, can add songs and remove his own, but the Pause button is disabled for him.

djs.body: A Lynx list, not a Discord role. DJs control playback in any control mode and skip right away even when vote skip is on. Only people who are in a voice channel of the server show up as candidates. Managers don't need to be on the list.
djs.example: With DJs only and vote skip on, you make Leo a DJ. From then on his Skip moves to the next song at once, while the rest of the channel still votes.

lynxChannel.body: The single text channel where every automatic Lynx message goes: Now playing, notices, jam and radio updates, and the message after a restart. Slash commands and buttons also only work there and in the command channels, except /invite, which works anywhere. Managers are exempt while "Managers can use Lynx in any channel" is on. When no channel is set, messages go to the channel where the last command was used, or to the voice channel's chat.
lynxChannel.example: You set #music. Someone uses /play in #general: Lynx asks them to use #music. The Now playing card, the notices and the message after a restart are always posted in #music.

commandChannels.body: Text channels (or the chat of a voice channel) where slash commands and the buttons on Lynx messages work. Leave it empty to allow every channel. With a Lynx channel set, commands work in the Lynx channel plus these. /invite always works anywhere, and managers are exempt while the managers toggle is on. Up to 25 channels.
commandChannels.example: No Lynx channel, command channels #bot-commands and #music. /play works in both; in #general Lynx answers that commands must be used in #bot-commands or #music.

voiceChannels.body: Voice channels where Lynx may play. Leave it empty to allow every voice channel. It applies to /play, the panel and the radio. Managers can play anywhere while the managers toggle is on.
voiceChannels.example: You allow only Lounge. Someone in Gaming uses /play: Lynx refuses and points them to Lounge. A manager in Gaming can still play there while the toggle is on.

managersExempt.body: On by default. While it is on, managers (owner, Administrator or Manage Server) can use commands, buttons and playback in any channel, whatever the channel lists say. Turn it off to make managers follow the same channel rules as everyone. /invite works anywhere either way.
managersExempt.example: The Lynx channel is #music. With the toggle on, an admin can use /queue in #staff. With it off, Lynx asks the admin to use #music too.

voteSkip.body: Off by default. When on, a skip from someone who can't skip directly counts as a vote, and the song is skipped once enough people in the channel voted. DJs, managers and whoever requested the current song skip right away. In DJs only mode, everyone else can vote too. Votes reset when the song changes.
voteSkip.example: Four people are listening and the rule is 50%. Leo presses Skip: 1 of 2 votes. Mia presses it too and the song is skipped.

voteMode.body: How the votes needed are set. Count is a fixed number of votes; Percent is a share of the people listening, rounded up. Either way at least 1 vote is needed and never more than the number of people listening. Deafened users don't vote and don't count as listeners.
voteMode.example: Count set to 3 with only 2 people listening: 2 votes are enough. Percent set to 50% with 5 listeners: 3 votes are needed.

votesNeeded.body: The number of votes needed to skip, from 1 to 25. If fewer people are listening than this number, every listener's vote is needed instead. People who leave the channel stop counting, which can make the existing votes enough.
votesNeeded.example: Set to 3 with 6 people listening: the third vote skips the song. If three of them leave after 2 votes, 2 of 3 listeners voted and the song is skipped.

percentNeeded.body: The share of people listening whose votes are needed to skip, from 1% to 100%, rounded up. Deafened users are not counted. When people join or leave, the votes needed are worked out again.
percentNeeded.example: Set to 50%: with 4 listeners 2 votes are needed, with 5 listeners 3. At 100%, every listener has to vote.

maxQueue.body: The most songs that can wait in the queue (the one playing does not count), from 1 to 5000. Default 500. When a playlist doesn't fit, only the songs that fit are added, and the radio never adds songs past it.
maxQueue.example: The limit is 100 and 90 songs are queued. Someone adds a 30-song playlist: the first 10 are added and the rest are left out.

defaultVolume.body: The volume a channel starts at when Lynx joins it, from 10% to 100%. Default 100%, which plays the audio untouched; Lynx never goes louder. Changing the volume during a session only affects that channel, and sessions restored after a restart keep their own volume.
defaultVolume.example: You set 60%. The next time Lynx joins a voice channel it plays at 60%. Someone turns it up to 80% there; other channels still start at 60%.

skipVotes.body: Vote skip is on in this server, so a skip from someone who isn't a DJ, a manager or the requester of this song counts as a vote. The bar shows the votes so far and how many are needed. Votes reset when the song changes; deafened users don't vote or count.
skipVotes.example: The bar shows 1 / 2. One more person in the channel presses Skip and the next song starts.

feedback.body: Tell the radio what you think of this song. Likes make it more likely to come back among your favorites; Dislikes keep it out of radio picks for everyone in the channel, but never skip it. Press again to clear your vote. Needs your listening history on.
feedback.example: You dislike a song that is playing. It keeps playing to the end, but the radio won't pick it again while you are in the channel.

ai.body: Songs marked AI were picked by the AI radio, not requested by a person. The line below the title says why it was picked, for example a favorite of yours or a song popular with people of similar taste.
ai.example: "Requested by Ana · Selected by AI" with "Because you like Daft Punk": Ana started the radio and it added this song because of her taste.

stop.body: Ends the session in this channel: the music stops, the queue is cleared, the radio stops and Lynx leaves the voice channel. In a jam, this channel leaves it first. It needs the right to control playback and can't be undone.
stop.example: You press Stop and confirm. Lynx leaves the channel and the queue is gone; the next /play starts a new session.

start.body: A jam lets several voice channels, in this server or others, hear the same queue at the same moment. Inviting turns this channel's queue into the shared one and gives you a link; whoever opens it gets the panel in their own voice channel and can join. Each channel keeps its own volume and Stop. Up to 8 channels; a jam ends when Lynx restarts.
start.example: You are in Lounge with a queue going and press Invite to jam. A friend opens the link from Gaming and joins: both channels now hear the same song at the same position.

active.body: The channels in this jam share one queue. The host channel decides the host settings, can remove channels and end the jam. Leaving gives a channel its own queue back. If the host channel leaves or empties, the host role passes to the oldest channel that still has people. A channel left empty for a few minutes drops out of the jam.
active.example: Gaming joined Lounge's jam with its own queue. When Gaming leaves, its saved queue comes back right where it was; Lounge keeps playing the jam.

settings.body: Only people in the host channel can change these, with the usual control rights of their server. Other channels of this server may join by default, other servers only if you allow it. Who edits the queue can be every channel or just the host channel; each server's DJ mode still applies. Closing keeps the channels already in and stops new ones from joining.
settings.example: You turn on Other servers and set Who edits the queue to Host channel. A friend's server can join and listen, but only people in your channel can add, skip or reorder.

add.body: Paste a link or type to search. Playlist, album and artist links add their songs up to the queue limit and are saved to your Playlists tab while your history is on. You need to be in the voice channel.
add.example: You paste a Spotify album link. Its songs go to the end of the queue and the album appears in your Playlists tab.

upNext.body: The songs waiting after the current one, in order. People who can control playback can drag to reorder, remove any song or clear the queue; everyone in the channel can remove the songs they added. The queue has a limit set by the managers (500 by default).
upNext.example: In DJs only mode, Leo added two songs. He can remove those two, but only a DJ or a manager can move them up the queue.

history.body: The last 20 songs that played in this channel during the current session, newest first, including songs that were skipped after they started. Songs jumped over or removed before playing are not listed. It is cleared when the session ends (Stop or Lynx leaving).
history.example: You skip a song halfway: it appears at the top of History, and you can add it again from there.

sources.body: Playlists and albums that have songs playing now or waiting in the queue, stacked like CDs. The list of the current song is always in front; the others wait behind it in queue order. Hover the stack to spread it out, and click a cover to open the list, save it to your playlists or jump to its next song in the queue. Single songs and radio picks are not part of any list.
sources.example: Ana adds her Spotify playlist and Leo his YouTube Music album. While Ana's songs play, her playlist is in front; when the first song of Leo's album starts, his album moves to the front.

list.body: Playlists, albums and artist pages you add with /play or in the Queue tab are saved here for you, in any server, while your history is on. When the list is full, the least recently used unpinned one makes room; pinned ones stay on top and are never replaced. Song lists are shared and kept for an hour; Refresh reads the playlist again now, once every 5 seconds, and too many refreshes block it for 5 minutes.
list.example: You saved 20 playlists and pinned 3. Adding a new album link removes the unpinned playlist you used the longest ago; the pinned ones stay.

card.body: Lyrics come from LRCLIB, matched by artist, title and length. Synced lyrics highlight the current line and follow the song; scrolling by hand pauses that for a few seconds. If you can control playback, clicking a line jumps there. Some songs only have plain lyrics and some have none.
card.example: A synced song is playing. You click the chorus line and the song jumps to it; the rest of the channel hears the jump too.

card.body: Keeps adding songs picked from your taste and the taste of the people in the channel whose history is on. The first song is queued right away and more are added when fewer than 3 are left. An optional prompt steers the picks. Starting it needs your history on; stopping it keeps the songs already queued. It can't run during a jam. In Discord, /ai also lets you choose the mix (mostly your favorites, balanced or new music) and turn off blending the channel's taste.
card.example: You start the radio with "calm music to study". It queues a first song at once and keeps adding similar ones until someone stops it.

picks.body: The songs the radio queued and why it picked each one, such as one of your favorites, an artist you like, a match for the prompt, or a song popular with people of similar taste. Up to 8 are shown.
picks.example: "Popular with listeners like you": people whose taste is close to yours play this song often.

taste.body: Your top genres and most played songs, built from your listening history and your likes. Only you can see it. Removing a song here deletes it from your history and counts as a Dislike, so the radio won't play it for you again; your taste is updated in the background.
taste.example: You remove a song you played a lot for a party. It leaves Most played, and your radio stops picking it.

privacy.body: With your history on, Lynx keeps the last 2000 different songs you requested and your Like and Dislike votes, for your radio and anonymous recommendations. Turning it off records nothing new and turns off Like, Dislike, /ai and playlist saving for you, but keeps what is already stored; use Delete my data for that.
privacy.example: You turn history off. Your next songs are not recorded and Like is disabled, but your saved playlists and taste stay until you delete them.

danger.body: Deletes, right away and for good, everything Lynx stored about your listening: history, Like and Dislike votes, taste and saved playlists. Your panel settings (language, theme, accent and the history switch) are kept.
danger.example: You delete your data. The Radio tab shows no taste yet, and your Playlists tab is empty until you add a new playlist.

source.cantSave: Only Spotify, YouTube, YouTube Music and Apple Music lists can be saved.
source.notUpcoming: No upcoming song of this list is in the queue.
source.cardHint_one: {{count}} list in what is playing and up next
source.cardHint_other: {{count}} lists in what is playing and up next
